description: Original bipartite_vertex_cover tests.rs and bounded models
state: Left adjacency rows G and right population R, combined vertices at most 1000000 and total stored edges at most 1000000; duplicate neighbors allowed.
cost: Enumerates sum over L,R<=3 of 2^(L*R)=689 graphs. Per graph, cover enumeration costs O(2^(L+R)*(L+E)); recursive matching explores at most (R+1)^L assignments. Separate resource cases store at most 1000001 edges or vertices. Fixed bounded test domain, not production complexity.
forward: Execute original bounded fixtures against independent oracles. Delegate resource/endpoint validation and matching to Hopcroft-Karp. Let Z start at unmatched left vertices and close under unmatched L-to-R edges and matched R-to-L edges. Return sorted (L minus ZL, ZR). König equality makes the cover cardinality equal to maximum matching cardinality. Test observations are named pass/fail assertions, not a semantic proof.
inverse: Test observation universe is fixture cases crossed with pass/fail and candidate answers. A pass is excluded if an independently enumerated cover minimum or stable-permutation constraint disagrees, if an expected boundary error differs, or if a repeated witness changes. Universe: valid graph/count inputs crossed with candidate sorted vertex subsets, together with typed validation errors. Absent behaviors include any uncovered edge, size unequal to maximum matching size, an out-of-range/duplicate/unsorted member, or selecting ZL on the left instead of its complement. With fixed deterministic matching and closure Z, every pair except (L minus ZL,ZR) is absent. Invalid inputs cannot return a cover; resource errors precede endpoint errors. This is an exact source-derived specification with partial finite correspondence, not a proof. Untested larger cases are outside the observed test transition universe.

A passing named test has many compatible production programs: arbitrary changes outside the exercised inputs, unused functions or histories can preserve all assertions. A failing optimality assertion retains every candidate answer violating the corresponding enumerated inequality, not a unique bug. For fixed cover (A,B), compatible antecedents are all bounded valid graphs whose deterministic alternating closure has ZL=L minus A and ZR=B; equivalently retain the matching/closure existential intermediate constrained by the actual deterministic Hopcroft-Karp traversal. Merely requiring A,B to cover edges is insufficient. Edge duplicates and extra isolated right vertices can have the same cover, so recovery is ambiguous. Empty graphs with zero or one right vertex both yield empty cover. Error fibers retain all graphs with the same first failing validation field.
limitations: Finite evidence, not proof; allocation failure unmodeled.
Partial syntax, no macro expansion or semantic AST.
